storyboard.claim: To understand the jar, we look at Teller's mother Arley.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller thinking about his mother, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the mother who is the source of the trauma.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names Arley on screen so the mother is identified.

storyboard.claim: Imagine a kid already an outcast at school, doing homework.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller, sad, the outcast phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the boy at school under the betrayal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the loneliness that makes the theft worse.

storyboard.claim: She was not checking homework; she was spying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller holding a magnifier, worried, reconnaissance on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Negates the homework reading with the spy reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magnifier shows scrutiny and spying, not study.

storyboard.claim: The host is horrified as a parent but respects Arley as a general.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, the respect phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the debate about Arley.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the reversal the next beats argue for.

storyboard.claim: Arley is a cold, brilliant, calculated tactician who made the impossible choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther pointing at the board, the tactician phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the host's case for Arley as a strategist.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point gesture is the board she plays.

storyboard.claim: The text contradicts the idea of Arley as a cold, rational tactician.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther pointing, the tactician phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns against the strategist reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the reading as the hosts' claim.

storyboard.claim: At the truce meeting, the descended crowns offer a ceasefire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther surprised at the table, the ceasefire on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the meeting the hosts mention.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stage is the temple setting of the truce.

storyboard.claim: The mortal rebellion has fought for the ceasefire over centuries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, the centuries phrase on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what the ceasefire means to the rebellion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the stake of the offer.

storyboard.claim: That is not a calculated military maneuver; it is raw maternal rage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, the maneuver phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the strategist reading from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected reading; the rage is the claim.

storyboard.claim: Teller's blood bond to his mother is unchosen and he grieves it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller slumped beside Luther, two bonded men.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the parallel between Teller and Luther.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pairs two men bound against their will.
storyboard.staging: Teller slumps in grief beside Luther.

storyboard.claim: The men's autonomy is taken because of the women they are bonded to.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller thinking, worried, in a stage setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why both men are dragged into the wars.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the cause of the lost autonomy.
storyboard.staging: Teller broods over the bond that controls him.

storyboard.claim: The thrones are political symbols, not just chairs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Burning thrones on the stage as symbols.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from spectacle to meaning.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the symbolism the thrones carry.
storyboard.staging: Thrones on the stage stand for power.

storyboard.claim: The thrones represent 900 years of systemic oppression.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Thrones on the stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the symbolism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the duration of the oppression.
storyboard.staging: Thrones carry the weight of centuries.

storyboard.claim: Burning the thrones alienates the aristocracy who fund the war.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage with the burned throne room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cost of the burning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the act that alienates the aristocracy.
storyboard.staging: Stage of the humiliation.

storyboard.claim: The aristocracy is the group Diem needs to fund the campaign.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage representing the aristocracy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names who is alienated.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies the funders.
storyboard.staging: Stage holds the aristocracy in view.

storyboard.claim: Tactically, burning the thrones is a terrible move.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Burned stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Verdict on the tactic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the narrator's tactical verdict.
storyboard.staging: Burned stage carries the verdict.

storyboard.claim: Diem's bond with Luther demands a new world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther thinking, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks why Diem burns the system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the bond to the politics.
storyboard.staging: Luther thinks over the bond.

storyboard.claim: Luther is a half-mortal outcast the elite system rejects.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther slumped, sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the system rejects Diem's bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names Luther's status.
storyboard.staging: Luther slumps, sad, outcast.

storyboard.claim: The consequence is an immediate public reckoning Diem faces.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage for the reckoning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leads into the street scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the reckoning.
storyboard.staging: Stage for the reckoning.

storyboard.claim: Diem walks the streets and meets Martha Hanover and the citizens of Lumnos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lumnos seen across a wide sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the throne room to the streets.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the meeting in the streets of Lumnos.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over the streets.

storyboard.claim: Grand destiny matters nothing to a person sweeping up the ashes of their home.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lumnos under a wide sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confronts the reality check.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the ashes the concrete cost.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over the ashes.

storyboard.claim: Leadership at its core is local.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lumnos under a wide sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the principle directly.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky, the principle in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Leadership is a physical contract: a leader must be present when fire falls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lumnos under a wide sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines leadership as presence.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over the contract.

storyboard.claim: Fancy titles are worthless when the leader is absent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Trophy icon on the stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the physical contract.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy shows the titles at stake.
storyboard.staging: Trophy on the stage.

storyboard.claim: Half of Fortos is reduced to rubble while Diem is absent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fortos under a wide sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves to Fortos.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the scale of the destruction.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over Fortos.

storyboard.claim: In politics, how things look matters more than the truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting for a political principle; no literal icon fits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the taunt works.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the political rule that makes the public gap dangerous.
storyboard.staging: Callout alone on the stage: the principle is the words, no icon reads it literally.

storyboard.claim: A crown must show up in person; citizens do not care about the magic behind the absence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wide Lumnos horizon, the people's view of their absent queen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the perception point to the bond between crown and people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates the citizens' view from the magical explanation.
storyboard.staging: Horizon with the callout: the magic is the wrong question for the people.

storyboard.claim: The descended see half mortals as impure abominations, while the mortals see them as oppressors.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract field; both views are carried by the words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes how each side views the outcasts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the descended view in the strongest words the narrator uses.
storyboard.staging: Callout alone on the abstract field: the words name the view.

storyboard.claim: Luther declares that half mortals step out of hiding into the light, which is unprecedented.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Open sky, the light the outcasts step into.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the meaning of the declaration.
storyboard.addedInformation: Light stands for leaving the shadows where they hid for their lives.
storyboard.staging: Sky with the callout: the light is the moment they leave the shadows.

storyboard.claim: Loyalty is not about pristine pure blood or a historic family name.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting; the rejected idea is struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Redefines loyalty after the declaration.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the blood-purity view of loyalty.
storyboard.staging: Callout struck through: the blood-purity idea is what the narrator rejects.
